I submitted all four parts. The item has no flaws: the strand directions and base pairs are consistent.

**Setup:** The fork moves right, and DNA polymerase can only add nucleotides to a 3' end, so new strands are built 5'→3'.

- **A: Bottom strand.** The bottom template runs 3'→5' from left to right. Its new strand runs 5'→3' from left to right, so it grows toward the moving fork and can be made continuously. That makes it the leading strand.
- **B: Why short fragments.** The top template runs 5'→3' from left to right, so its new strand must run 3'→5' from left to right. Because polymerase only builds 5'→3', this strand has to grow leftward, away from the fork. As the fork opens more template, polymerase has to start again with a new primer each time. This makes short Okazaki fragments, which DNA ligase later joins. This is the lagging strand.
- **C: New strand on the top template.** Pair each base with its complement (A with T, G with C). The new strand, read left to right, is **3'-CTAGGAGCG-5'**.
- **D: Semiconservative.** The new double helix has one old strand (the top template, 5'-GATCCTCGC-3') and one new strand (3'-CTAGGAGCG-5'). Each daughter DNA molecule keeps half of the parent molecule and adds one newly made strand.

answers.final_answer: Bottom template strand

answers.final_answer: DNA polymerase only builds 5'->3', so the new strand on the top template grows away from the fork and is made in short Okazaki fragments, each started by a new primer and later joined by ligase.
